candidate.answerReason: The brick's volume is 8000 cubic centimeters. Spread over the aquarium's 4000-square-centimeter base, this produces a 2 cm rise, to a depth of 42 cm, choice D.

methods.label: Use the brick's displaced volume
methods.explanation:
Resting on its base at the bottom of the aquarium, the brick is only \(10\) cm tall, so it is completely below the initial \(40\)-cm water level. It therefore displaces its full volume,
\[
40\cdot20\cdot10=8000\text{ cm}^3.
\]
The aquarium's base area is
\[
100\cdot40=4000\text{ cm}^2.
\]
Each centimeter of rise provides \(4000\text{ cm}^3\) of additional volume below the surface. Since the amount of water stays the same, the rise is
\[
\frac{8000}{4000}=2\text{ cm}.
\]
The final depth is \(40+2=42\) cm, below the aquarium's \(50\)-cm height, so no water overflows. The answer is \(\boxed{2\text{ cm}}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).

needsNewNodes.name: Liquid displacement and water-level change
needsNewNodes.description: Relate the volume of a fully submerged solid to the increase in occupied volume below a liquid surface. In a container with constant horizontal cross-sectional area and no overflow, that area multiplied by the level rise equals the submerged solid's volume.
needsNewNodes.reason: The catalog covers prism volumes but lacks the displacement relationship connecting an immersed solid's volume to a liquid-level rise.
